BACKGROUND

Enhancing public safety and quality of life is a top priority for all. To support this, effective
security operations are implemented to deter crime and suspicious activities at Housing
Authority and City-owned facilities.

The Housing Authority oversees three mobile home parks and four apartment
complexes, each with a security program that includes unarmed security guard services,
access control, parking enforcement, asset protection, and crime deterrence through
observation.

The City provides security across all facilities, including the Civic Center, Palmdale
Transportation Center, park-and-ride locations, neighborhood houses, and parks. By
enhancing security, the City aims to improve residents’ daily lives by fostering safety,
reducing crime, and creating a secure environment for people to work, live and play.

DISCUSSION

A Request for Proposal (RFP) No. 23-002-4400 for Unarmed Security Guard Services
was released on December 12, 2023, to align and consolidate citywide security efforts.
Notifications were distributed through PlanetBids to 164 security service vendors, and 18
complete bids were received, with no bidders from the Antelope Valley.

Interviews were held with the top four bidders on March 14, 2024, and Good Guard
Security, Inc. was one of the top-rated candidates. While based in Chatsworth, CA, its
goal is to recruit and employ from within the Antelope Valley.

Master Services Agreement No. A-9189 for the Housing Authority will house Project
Authorizations A through G. Master Services Agreement No. A-9190 will house Project
Authorizations A and B. All agreements/project authorizations are attached for reference.

and/or licensed security guards for the protection of the Housing Authority of the City of
Palmdale’s (Housing Authority) employees, the public, and property. Good Guard
Security, Inc. shall plan, schedule, and coordinate with the Housing Authority and On-Site
Property Management to ensure the effective performance of all services described
herein. The quality and experience of security guards and the services provided will be
critical elements of the contract.

  laws, rules, and regulations, including but not limited to those regarding wages,
  and cover all rest and meal periods to ensure continuous coverage.
  • Good Guard Security, Inc. shall agree and ensure that security personnel fully
  perform their duties in accordance with City-imposed policies, procedures, and
  conditions for continued service at this account.
  o Good Guard Security, Inc. shall ensure that security personnel are fully
  aware of the political sensitivities that exist in a municipal government. Good
  Guard Security, Inc. shall immediately transfer/remove security personnel
  from the account at the Housing Authority’s request.
  • Good Guard Security, Inc. shall provide standard uniforms to security personnel.
  o Security guards are to be dressed in appropriate uniforms that comply with
  the “name and patch” requirements of the State of California Department of
  Consumer Affairs for security guards. Uniforms are to be neat, clean,
  pressed, and lint-free. Uniforms are to include dress or leather work shoes
  that are clean, in good repair, and color coordinated with the uniform. No
  tennis or athletic shoes are permitted.
  o This also includes a visual depiction of uniforms as part of the proposal,
  including any overcoats, jackets, headgear, and photo ID badges.
  • Good Guard Security, Inc. shall ensure all security personnel have proper
  communication equipment (radios, cell phones, etc.).
  • Good Guard Security, Inc. shall ensure that security guards are provided with or
  bring their own water or hydration drinks for their assignment and are supported in
  all weather conditions.

  point of contact for the Housing Authority and who will ensure all work tasks are
  performed by each security guard and staff to meet contract obligations. The
  Supervisor/Manager shall coordinate all phases of security services.
  • The Supervisor/Manager shall work continuously with the Housing Authority
  representative to improve or modify the schedules, service model, and reporting
  protocols as needed.
  • The Supervisor/Manager shall address all issues relating to this contract, staffing,
  performance, etc.
   •  Good Guard Security, Inc. shall not replace the Supervisor/Manager unless prior
  written notice is provided to and approved by the Housing Authority.

  periodically check security guard staff during assigned shifts. The assigned
  supervisor shall provide the Housing Authority Representative with any identified
  issues and any resolution, as necessary.

  criteria, please refer to the “Reporting and Notification” section.

  for any services or any other labor, supervision, or material that is in excess of the
  Scope of Services.

  through checks and balances, audits, and/or inspections.
  •  Good Guard Security, Inc. shall, at the firm’s expense, have all assigned guards
  complete Good Guard Security, Inc. established training program, and shall make
  evidence of completion of the training available upon request. In addition, Good
  Guard Security, Inc. must provide a copy of their training plan/schedule.
  •  Good Guard Security, Inc. will conduct personal background checks on all
  personnel before they are assigned work under the Award Contract with the
  Housing Authority. Background checks must include fingerprinting. The Housing
  Authority reserves the right to review all background checks and to conduct
  security clearances on all personnel assigned. The Housing Authority may verify
  each license and obtain Good Guard Security, Inc.’s complaint history from the
  Department of Consumer Affairs, Bureau of Collection, and Investigative Services.

  Guard Registration (California Guard Card) of the California State Department of
  Consumer Affairs, Bureau of Collections, and Investigations. The Security guard
  shall act as a polite and professional “ambassador” for the Housing Authority,
  educating visitors on current site rules and regulations and requesting compliance.
  • Upon arrival, security guards shall contact Site Management personnel to confirm
  the guard is onsite.
  • Security guards’ appearance, personal hygiene, attitude, courtesy, and job
  knowledge need to present a favorable image. No smoking, reading unauthorized
  material, eating, or grooming shall be permitted while guards are in public view.
  • Security guards shall arrive in uniform provided by Good Guard Security, Inc.,
  before arriving on site. The uniform must have the Good Guard Security, Inc.
  name. A photo ID badge is to be worn at all times. Security guards shall maintain
  CPR and First Aid Training certification and remain certified to remain compliant.
  No personal phone calls will be permitted, except in an emergency.
  • All Security personnel are responsible for documenting any security incidents in a
  formal report and shall provide electronic copies to the Housing Authority. Further
  criteria are noted in the “Reporting and Notification” section below.
  • Security guards shall be adequately trained and experienced in their specific
  duties, and in addition, the use of all-purpose fire extinguishers, drug/narcotics
   identification, bomb threat situations, the avoidance of violent situations, and be
  specifically trained for each piece of security equipment carried or used.
•  Security guards shall protect the safety of persons and properties on site.
•  Security guards shall always be clearly visible when on foot patrol.
•  Security Guards shall not be permitted to carry a weapon of any type.
•  Security Guards shall not be permitted to carry or possess any unauthorized
  equipment such as firearms, knives, batons, Tasers, chemical agents, concealed
  weapons, or any other items, not specifically approved in the Contract.
•  Security Guard must be of a temperament to work and communicate with adults,
  teens, and children of all ages and be capable of controlling a crowd in all
  circumstances.
•  Security guard shall prohibit entry into secured sites by anyone other than persons
  with authorized access to the premises and assist/escort patrons on/off the
  property as necessary.
•  Good Guard Security, Inc. will fully cooperate with the Housing Authority, City of
  Palmdale, Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department, and any other public agency,
  in addition to making any assigned security guard available to said
  agencies/entities in the event of any investigation.
•  Good Guard Security, Inc. shall be responsible for any loss or damage to property,
  including money securities, merchandise, fixtures, and equipment belonging to the
  Housing Authority if the Contractor caused any such loss or damage.

C. Security Guard Patrol Vehicle Requirements/Duties
• When required, as needed, or as requested, Good Guard Security, Inc. shall
  provide a clearly marked and professional Patrol Vehicle. Vehicle type, markings,
  lights, etc. are to be of a type approved by the Housing Authority.
• Patrol Vehicles shall be equipped with a heavy-duty/rechargeable flashlight, traffic
  cones, flares, a first aid kit, a blanket, and a fire extinguisher.
• Security Guards operating Patrol Vehicles shall conduct patrols in Good Guard
  Security, Inc.-provided vehicles. Patrol Security Guards shall have valid Class “C”
  California driver’s licenses.

D. Reporting and Notification
• Security guards shall log and report all serious incidents to the Onsite Management
  and Housing Authority Representative.
  o Items to be documented include, but are not limited to, suspicious persons,
  security breaches, system failures, facility maintenance issues, safety
  hazards, any bomb threats, criminal activity, or incidents that occur to any
  member of the public.
  o These forms should be used to document any damage, such as graffiti or
  vandalism, noted at any of the Housing Authority facilities.
  o Security personnel shall document any security incidents on the incident
  report form and provide electronic copies to the Onsite Management and
  Housing Authority Representative.
 •  The Vendor must have a patrol monitoring system in place to allow security guards
  to scan assigned QR-code checkpoints located at Housing Authority facility
  locations including building entrances, doors, window frames, etc.
  o The function is to be used on regular patrol, for tracking, and to generate
  real-time reports. Special events would be requested on an as-needed
  basis.
  o Guard tours are to be monitored by Good Guard Security, Inc., the Onsite
  Management, and the Housing Authority Representative remotely and sent
  by email to ensure required patrols are being conducted.
E. Customer Service and After-Hours Notification
• Good Guard Security, Inc. is required to have a dedicated after-hours notification
  line monitored and answered by an employee who can dispatch crews should an
  after-hour emergency or urgent issue occur.
F. Hours of Operation
• Work hours vary by facility and times are subject to change at any time. The
  Contractor will be notified by the Onsite Management or the Housing Authority
  Representative of any changes to department hours or any adjustments needed
  to be made to the existing schedule prior to implementation.

G. Requests from the Public
• Good Guard Security, Inc. and its security guards are prohibited from taking direct
  requests from any residents, visitors to the facilities, or any other organizations.
  The security guard will make every effort to politely inform the requesting individual
  or party to contact Onsite Management or the Housing Authority Representative.

H. Requests from the Media
• Good Guard Security, Inc. and its security guards shall not speak to the media on
  the Housing Authority’s behalf without prior approval. All media inquiries should be
  directed to the City’s Public Information Officer (PIO) or City Representative.

  SCOPE OF WORK

The Contractor shall provide appropriately equipped and well-trained, certified, and/or licensed
security guards for the protection of the City’s employees, the public, and property, and shall
plan, schedule, and coordinate with the City of Palmdale to ensure the effective performance of
all services described herein. The quality and experience of security guards and the services
provided will be critical elements of the contract, particularly in the following “Scope of Work
(Specifications).”

A. Contractor Service Requirements:
   The Contractor shall comply with all applicable federal, state, and local laws, rules, and
  regulations, including but not limited to those regarding wages, and cover all rest and
  meal periods to ensure continuous coverage.
   The Contractor shall agree and ensure that security personnel fully perform their duties in
  accordance with City-imposed policies, procedures, and conditions for continued service
  at this account.
  o The Contractor shall ensure that security personnel are fully aware of the political
  sensitivities that exist in a municipal government.
  o The Contractor shall immediately transfer/remove security personnel from the
  account at the City’s request.
   The Contractor shall provide standard uniforms to security personnel.
  o Security guards are to be dressed in appropriate uniforms that comply with the “name
  and patch” requirements of the State of California Department of Consumer Affairs
  for security guards. Uniforms are to be neat, clean, pressed, and lint-free. Uniforms
  are to include dress or leather work shoes that are clean, in good repair, and color
  coordinated with the uniform. No tennis or athletic shoes are permitted.
  o This also includes a visual depiction of uniforms, including any overcoats, jackets,
  headgear, and photo ID badge.
   The Contractor shall ensure all security personnel have proper communication equipment
  (radios, cell phones, etc.).
   The Contractor shall ensure that security guards are provided with or bring their
  water/hydration drinks for events and are provided support for all weather conditions.
   The Contractor shall designate a Supervisor/Manager who will be the point of contact for
  the City and who will ensure all work tasks are performed by each security guard and
  staff to meet contract obligations.
  o The Supervisor/Manager shall coordinate all phases of security services.
  o The Supervisor/Manager shall work continuously with the City representative to
  improve or modify the schedules, service model, and reporting protocols as needed.
  o The Supervisor/Manager shall address all issues relating to this contract, staffing,
  performance, etc.
  o The Contractor shall not replace the Supervisor/Manager unless prior written notice is
  given to and approved by the City.
   The Contractor shall provide supervision of on-site security guards and must provide
  sporadic checks of security guard staff during assigned shifts. The assigned supervisor
  shall provide the City Representative with any issues identified and any resolutions, as
  necessary.

  Exhibit A

    The Contractor shall offer a patrol motoring system. Please refer to the “Reporting and
  Notification” section for further system criteria.
   The Contractor shall not be entitled to be paid or reimbursed by the City for any services
  or any other labor, supervision, or material that is in excess of the Scope of Services.
   The Contractor shall ensure security guards provide exceptional service through checks
  and balances, audits, and/or inspections.
   The Contractor shall, at the firm’s expense, have all assigned guards complete the
  Contractor’s established training program and shall make evidence of such training
  available upon request.
   The Contractor will conduct personal background checks on all personnel before they are
  assigned work under the Award Contract with the City of Palmdale. Background checks
  must include fingerprinting. The City of Palmdale reserves the right to review all
  background checks and to conduct security clearances on all personnel assigned. The
  City of Palmdale may verify each license and obtain a complaint history of the successful
  Proposer from the Department of Consumer Affairs, Bureau of Collection, and
  Investigative Services.
B. Security Guard Requirements
   All unarmed security guards shall meet the requirements, including a valid Security
  Guard Registration (California Guard Card) of the California State Department of
  Consumer Affairs, Bureau of Collections, and Investigations. The Security guard shall act
  as a polite and professional “ambassador” for the City, educating visitors on current site
  rules and regulations and requesting compliance.
   Designated City representative shall have access to verify arrival/departure times from
  assigned locations.
   Security guards’ appearance, personal hygiene, attitude, courtesy, and job knowledge
  need to present a favorable image. No smoking, reading unauthorized material, eating, or
  grooming shall be permitted while guards are in public view.
  o Security guards shall arrive in uniform provided by the Contractor before arriving
  on site.
  o The uniform must have the Contractor’s name. A photo ID badge is to be always
  worn.
   No personal phone calls will be permitted except in an emergency.
   All Security personnel are responsible for documenting any security incidents in a formal
  report and shall provide electronic copies to the City. Further criteria are noted in the
  “Reporting and Notification” section below.
   Security guards shall escort City staff as requested. A dispatch number shall be provided
  to accommodate escort services upon award of contract services.
   Security guards shall be adequately trained and experienced in their specific duties, and
  in addition, the use of all-purpose fire extinguishers, drug/narcotics identification, bomb
  threat situations, the avoidance of violent situations, and be specifically trained for each
  piece of security equipment carried or used.
  o Security guards shall maintain CPR and First Aid Training certification and remain
  certified to remain compliant.
   Security guards shall protect the safety of persons and properties on site.
   Security guards shall always be clearly visible when on foot patrol.
   Security Guards shall not be permitted to carry a weapon of any type.
   Agrmt No. A-9190-A
  Exhibit A

  o  Security personnel shall not be permitted to carry or possess any unauthorized
  equipment such as firearms, knives, batons, Tasers, chemical agents, concealed
  weapons, or any other items not specifically approved in the Contract.
   Security Guard must have the temperament to work and communicate with adults, teens,
  and children of all ages and be capable of controlling a crowd in all circumstances.
   Security guard shall prohibit entry into secured sites by anyone other than persons with
  authorized access to the premises and assist/escort patrons on/off the property as
  necessary.
   The Contractor will fully cooperate with the City of Palmdale, Los Angeles County
  Sheriff’s Department, and any other public agency, in addition to making any assigned
  security guard available to said agencies/entities in the event of any investigation.
   The Contractor shall be responsible for any loss or damage to property, including money
  securities, merchandise, fixtures, and equipment belonging to the City if the Contractor
  caused any such loss or damage.
C. Security Guard Patrol Vehicle Requirements/Duties
   When required, as needed, or as requested, the Contractor shall provide a clearly marked
  and professional Patrol Vehicle.
  o Vehicle type, markings, lights, etc., are to be of a type approved by the City.
   Patrol Vehicles shall be equipped with a heavy-duty/Rechargeable flashlight, Traffic
  Cones, Flares, a First Aid Kit, a Blanket, and a Fire Extinguisher.
   Security Guards operating Patrol Vehicles shall conduct patrols in Contractor-provided
  vehicles.
Patrol Security Guards shall have valid Class “C” California driver’s licenses.
D. Reporting and Notification
   Security guards shall log and report all serious incidents, as defined by the City.
  o Items to be documented include, but are not limited to, suspicious persons, security
  breaches, system failures, facility maintenance issues, safety hazards, any bomb
  threats, criminal activity, or incidents that occur to any member of the public.
  o The Contractor’s patrol monitoring system should report electronically to the City’s
  reporting system for any damage, such as graffiti or vandalism, noted at any of the
  city facilities.
  o Security personnel shall document any security incidents on the Contractor’s
  reporting platform/software and provide electronic copies to the City.
 The Vendor must have a patrol monitoring system in place to allow security guards to scan
  assigned QR-code checkpoints located at City entrances, doors, window frames, etc.
  o The function is to be used on regular patrol, for tracking, and to generate real-time
  reports.
  o Guard tours are to be monitored by the Contractor & City representative remotely and
  sent by email to ensure required patrols are being conducted.
   Customer Service and After-Hours Notification
  o The Contractor is required to have a dedicated after-hours notification line monitored
  and answered by an employee who can dispatch crews should an after-hour
  emergency or urgent issue occur.
E. Hours of Operation
   Work hours vary by department, and times are subject to change at any time. Events,
  dates, and times will vary throughout the year. The Contractor will be notified by the
  Department City Representative of any changes to department hours or adjustments to the
  existing schedule prior to implementation.

 F. Requests from the Public
   The Contractor and its security guards are prohibited from taking direct requests from
  any residents, park patrons, or any other organizations. The security guard will make
  every effort to politely inform the requesting individual or party to contact the City
  Staff/Representative.
 G. Requests from the Media
   The Contractor and its security guards shall not speak to the media on the City’s behalf
  without prior approval. All media inquiries should be directed to the City’s Public
  Information Officer (PIO) or City Representative.

BACKGROUND

Treasurer shall prepare and present monthly and quarterly reports on investments to
the City Manager/Executive Director and the City Council/Directors. The reports shall
detail the type of investment, issuer’s name, purchase date, maturity date, amount of
deposit, and interest rate. This information shall be provided for all City and Successor
Agency pooled investments and for Certificates of Participation, Revenue Bonds, Tax
Allocation Bonds, Assessment Districts, and Community Facilities District accounts
managed by outside Fiscal Agents.

The monthly investment reports provide a synopsis of the City and Successor Agency's
investment activity. They provide information on assets, allocations, average maturities,
yields, and book valuations. The interest rates presented are the most current rates
available as of the date of this report.

based on closing prices for the related investment as of the date of this report. This

DISCUSSION

Compliance with Investment Policy

For November, the City’s invested portfolio totaled $322,732,852, a decrease of
$11,745,486 from the previous month and an increase of $16,604,784 compared to the
prior year. The monthly decrease resulted from the transferring of funds between the
City’s operating and LAIF accounts to pay for ongoing operating expenses.

The par value of Successor Agency’s portfolio as of November was $5,493,576. The
balance increased by $967,572 from the prior month due to the transfer of funds from
the City’s operating account to fund the upcoming debt service payment, due December
1, 2024.

All investments meet criteria appropriate to Section 8 of the Investment Policy. The
portfolios are based on a combination of various investments, including CDs, Corporate
Notes, US Treasury Securities, and Government Agency Paper, each adhering to
portfolio percentage limitations.

The Finance Division is the custodian for the City and Successor Agency’s investment
portfolio and follows the three main principles of both entities’ investment policies: 1)
Investment in financial instruments that mitigate the risk of monetary losses stemming
from market fluctuations; 2) Establish and maintain a portfolio that has sufficient liquidity
to allow the City and Successor Agency to meet all anticipated cash requirements; and,
3) Seek out investment instruments that provide a competitive market rate of return.

Liquidity

One core approach the Finance Division focuses on is providing liquidity to meet the
City and Successor Agency’s operational requirements. Thus, the City invests in two
pooled funds, Local Agency Investment Fund (LAIF) and the California Asset
Management Program (CAMP). These are intended for daily operational activities and
can be used during economic uncertainties for ongoing operating and maintenance
needs. The pooled funds provide a higher liquidity ratio to ensure the City and Successor
Agency meet cash flow requirements.

The City's LAIF balance at the end of November was $100,310,289, a decrease of
$10,000,000 due to the transfer of funds between LAIF and the City’s general checking
account to fund ongoing operating expenses for the month.

The Successor Agency’s LAIF balance at the end of November was $3,813,014, with
no changes from the prior month.

SUBJECT:  APPROVE ENERGY FOR PALMDALE’S INDEPENDENT CHOICE’S
  (EPIC) 2023 POWER CONTENT LABEL (PCL) AND ATTESTATION

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the City Council approve EPIC’s 2023 PCL and Attestation.

BACKGROUND

The attestation specified under California’s Power Source Disclosure (PSD) Program
requires the governing council of a public agency providing retail electric service to
endorse the accuracy of the previous year’s annual report and PCL submitted to the
California Energy Commission (CEC). For EPIC, such attestations will be based on the
California Choice Energy Authority’s (CalChoice) technical review, and they will address
the 2023 Annual Reports and PCL prepared for the EPIC Community Choice
Aggregation (CCA) program.

The PCL is analogous to a nutrition label, conveying information regarding the various
power sources/products procured for each retail electricity customer. California’s retail
electricity sellers, including EPIC, will each have unique PCLs based on internally
adopted procurement policies, statutory procurement mandates, and related power
purchases completed during the reporting year.

The PCL format is highly prescriptive, offering little flexibility to retail sellers when
presenting such information to customers. The CEC administers these requirements
under California’s PSD Program.

DISCUSSION

Information presented in each PCL includes the proportionate share of total energy
supply related to specific fuel sources/resource categories, including both renewable
and conventional generating technologies. An emission factor for each retail service

offering, as calculated using the CEC’s prescribed methodology, is also provided in the
PCL. It is very common for most retail electricity sellers to utilize “unspecified power”.
For example, suppose a retail seller procures a certain percentage of its energy
requirements from the market at large (sources of power that cannot be traced back to
a specific generator), the PCL must identify such purchases as unspecified sources of
power.

In 2002, Senate Bill (SB) 1078 established California’s Renewable Portfolio Standard
(RPS). The RPS established a timetable outlining the minimum percentage of renewable
energy provided to ratepayers with the ultimate goal of providing 100 percent renewable
energy by 2045 (as established in 2018 through the passage of SB 100). Renewable
fuel sources may include biomass and waste, hydroelectricity, solar, geothermal, and
wind. Per RPS and internally adopted planning targets, EPIC procured a substantial
portion of its electric energy supply from generating resources utilizing various
renewable fuel sources in 2023. For EPIC Power customers, 41.3% of the total energy
supply was sourced from RPS-eligible (CEC-certified) renewable energy resources in
2023. When comparing percentages in Schedule 3 of the PSD report and PCL, please
note that these distinct reports apply different numeric rounding conventions so
percentages may not match exactly. For EPIC Power100 customers, 100% of energy
deliveries were sourced from renewable energy resources, including bundled and
unbundled renewable energy products.

Recent changes to power source disclosure regulations have also altered how certain
renewable energy purchases must be reported/reflected on the PCL. More specifically,
“unbundled” renewable energy certificates (renewable energy attributes that are
sold/purchased separately from associated electric power) must now be displayed
outside the area in which “bundled” renewable energy purchases (renewable energy
attributes that are sold/purchased with associated electric power) are reported. This
adaptation to the PCL format may result in some customer confusion, as determining
the total quantity of renewable energy purchased on behalf of each customer now
requires the summation of two values: “Eligible Renewable” plus “Percentage of Retail
Sales Covered by Retired Unbundled RECs”. EPIC is prepared to answer related
questions, should they arise.

To fulfill its PSD Program reporting obligations for 2023, EPIC as a public agency, must
provide the CEC with the City Council’s attestation regarding the accuracy of information
included in each annual Power Source Disclosure Report (submitted to the CEC earlier
in 2024, according to the applicable reporting deadline) and PCL, consistent with the
following element of PSD Program regulations.

RECOMMENDATION

Discuss proposed Ordinance No. 1649 amending Palmdale Municipal Code (PMC)
Section 2.08.040 relating to the setting of regular meeting day and time of the City Council
and adopt or reject as necessary.

BACKGROUND

Conducting effective City Council meetings is indispensable. Council meetings are the
platform for the Council to conduct the City’s corporate business affairs with the various
businesses, developers, contractors, finance firms, and lobbyists that require focused City
Council attention. The meetings also allow the Council to address policy and
administration issues, such as contracts and approvals. The meetings provide a platform
for elected and appointed people to unite in making key decisions on various aspects
such as health, agriculture, environment, education, transport, development, and safety.

The measure of a City Council meeting’s effectiveness dramatically impacts the outcome
of positive progress and effective decision-making.

It is also important to address some of the challenges arising from ineffective meetings,
leading to intense and critical problems requiring prolonged solutions. Ineffectiveness
contributes to:
    Poor focus on critical issues and matters;
    Slowed development and growth;
    Disorganized meetings and events;
    Conflicts and delays in meaningful discussions; and,
    Inadequate characterization of public policies.

DISCUSSION

A meeting day and time change is being proposed to maximize the effectiveness of
Palmdale’s council meetings.

The proposed change in the day would align Palmdale City Council meetings with the day
of the week (Tuesday) on which most legislative bodies hold their meetings.

Each version of the Ordinance provides a different time for the Council to consider: 1)
The time change to a 2:00 pm closed session and a 3:00 pm regular meeting allows the
City Council to conduct City business during hours that align with the corporate,
development, legislative, and business community. This will allow the City Council, staff,
businesses, and community to conduct business during standard working hours instead
of late into the evening, which can negatively affect health and wellbeing and lead to
decisions being compromised due to fatigue; and 2) The 5:00 pm time would keep the
time as currently set. The proposed changes to the PMC are as follows:

Version one of Ordinance 1649:

Regular meetings of the City Council will be held on the first and third Tuesday of each
month. Meetings of the City Council shall be held at 38300 Sierra Highway, Suite B,
Palmdale, California. The closed session will begin at 2:00 pm, followed by the meeting
at 3:00 pm. If all closed session items are not addressed by 3:00 pm, the closed session
will resume after the regular meeting. If all matters on the agenda for any regular meeting
have not been considered by the City Council by the hour of 10:30 pm, or such earlier or
later time as may be fixed by a majority vote of the City Council, then the regular meeting
may be adjourned to the next succeeding Tuesday, at the same time and the exact
location, unless a different day, time or location is specified in the order of adjournment.
When so adjourned, each adjourned meeting shall be a regular meeting for all purposes.
At least twice a year, the City Council shall meet to receive and/or present recognitions
to and/or from the community. Notice of all meetings of the City Council, whether regular,
adjourned, special, or emergency, will be given in the manner required by state statute
(Brown Act or successor law). When a regular Tuesday meeting of the City Council falls
on an election day or a national or state holiday and City offices are scheduled to be
closed. Such meetings shall not be held and will be deemed adjourned for all purposes
with no further action required by the City Council or the City Clerk except such written
notices of adjournment as may be required by law. The ordinances codified in this section
shall take effect 30 days after adoption.

 I.  Intent of the City Council

  a) The City Council is a strict supporter of the open meeting law known and referenced
  as the Brown Act. The Brown Act is a transparency-driven law that requires all non-
  privileged City business to be conducted in public so that all can follow, participate in
  and communicate upon the business of the City.

  As business meetings under the Brown Act, it is clear that the intent and focus of public
